answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so influence decays when paths repeatedly cross sparse boundaries. A sybil cluster—whether labeled grove, saffron, or spiral—typically has low conductance: its few honest-facing edges form a sparse external cut. Conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap the probability mass, and hence aggregate voting weight, that the cluster can capture, even with many internal identities.
